definitions.explanation: A formal indication of choice in an election or decision. Also used as a counter for votes.

examples.japanese: {選挙|せんきょ}で{一票|いっぴょう}を{投|とう}じた。
examples.english: I cast one vote in the election.
examples.notes: 一票を投じる = to cast a vote

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{最多|さいた}{票|ひょう}で{当選|とうせん}した。
examples.english: She was elected with the most votes.

examples.japanese: {票|ひょう}を{数|かぞ}える{作業|さぎょう}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: The work of counting votes continues.

notes:
USAGE: {票|ひょう} is used both as a noun meaning vote/ballot and as a counter for votes.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{一票|いっぴょう} (one vote)
・{票|ひょう}を{入|い}れる (to vote)
・{票|ひょう}を{投|とう}じる (to cast a vote)
・{票|ひょう}を{集|あつ}める (to gather votes)
・{得票|とくひょう} (votes obtained)

COUNTER NOTE: As a counter, the reading changes: {一票|いっぴょう}, {二票|にひょう}, {三票|さんびょう}, etc.
